newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac slightly up in opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac slightly up in opinion poll.

text.p: The popularity of French President Jacques Chirac has risen slightly but Prime Minister Alain Juppe's has continued to drop, according to an opinion poll released on Friday.

The BVA survey for the weekly Paris-Match showed 58 per cent of those asked had a poor opinion of the president, down two points from last month's similar poll. Thirty-five percent had a good opinion, the same figure as November. Those with no opinion were seven per cent compared to five per cent last month.
Those who had a poor opinion of Juppe were 72 per cent compared to 73 per cent last month but those with a good opinion of the prime minister fell two points to a new record low of 20 per cent.
Eight per cent of those asked had no opinion on Juppe. They were five per cent the previous month.
The poll was carried out between December 12, the day of an interview given by Chirac to French television, and December 14 among 866 people.

Another poll by CSA for Christian weekly La Vie showed 55 per cent of those asked did not trust the president, up two points from last month, while 63 per cent did not trust Juppe against 62 per cent in the previous simlar poll.
The CSA poll was carried among 1,001 people the day after Thursday's interview in which Chirac gave Juppe his full support and ruled out a cabinet reshuffle.
Both polls were carried out before Juppe's book, called "Entre Nous" (Between Ourselves) and complaining that people are unfair to him, went on sale on Tuesday.
